Definition: to approach (causatively, bring near) for whatever purpose
KeyPassages: Exodus 3:5; Leviticus 16:1; Deuteronomy 4:11; Psalms 65:4; Isaiah 41:1; Jeremiah 30:21
BiblicalUsage: To draw near is the word for approaching God and approaching the altar: draw not nigh hither, put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground; the priests drew near to offer; the people stood afar off and came not near. The psalmist says, blessed is the man whom Thou choosest, and causest to approach unto Thee, that he may dwell in Thy courts.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe drawing near is the whole of worship in one word, and the wonder is that God causes the approach, we do not force it. That is why the ground is holy and the courts are open: He draws us near, and we come.
